segments.text: In every region of the world there is a ritual or a festival unique to that land
They reflect the people's view of the world, their sense of religion and their relationship with nature
In Japan, the first trine visit of the year
Setsuban Obon and the festivals of each region
Are still carefully kept
The Jien Festival of Kyoto has a history of more than a thousand years
And the Nebuta Festival of Aomori fills the night streets with passion
Such traditions are not nearly a habit of the past
It is also a place where the people of a community
Confirm their own identity, who they are in the world
There are rites of passage that celebrate birth, adulthood, marriage and death
These are events in which the whole community stands beside a person
At a turning point of life and sends them on toward a new stage
But the wave of globalization is making the unique cultures of each place uniform
Young people move to the cities and the bearers of local festivals continue to decline
Many traditional crafts have already disappeared
On the other hand, there is also a movement
To preserve such fading cultures
Unesco registers, but traditional cultures
Of various regions of the world
As intangible heritage
Japanese food, no theater
And the making of Japanese paper
Are among these tradition
Is not a relic of the past
It is a living gift that we
The people who live now
Hand down to the next generation
